name: Farmhouse Inn Sonoma
positioning: Intimate country inn on six quiet acres in Sonoma's Russian River Valley, between vineyards, redwoods and the coast, founded by fifth-generation Sonomans
best_for: Couples who want a cottage or barn suite with a fireplace and a soaking tub
Wine lovers who want the concierge to arrange vineyard tours and tastings
Travelers who want a spa that uses locally grown ingredients

facts.text: Farmhouse Inn is a hideaway in Sonoma's Russian River Valley.
The inn is set on six quiet acres between vineyards, redwoods and the coast.
The inn feels more like a private country home than a hotel.
Farmhouse Inn was founded in 2001 by brother and sister Joe and Catherine Bartolomei, fifth-generation Sonomans whose family farm is nearby.
The Barn One Bedroom Suite, tucked furthest back on the property, has a separate sitting room and a wide patio warmed by a dual fireplace.
Many Wellness Barn treatments spotlight locally grown and sourced ingredients, and the menu includes a CBD and gem stone bathing ritual.
Fitness options include a walking path beneath the trees, a Peloton bike and free weights, and private sessions the team can arrange.
The property has a swimming pool and gardens with roses in late spring and early summer.
There is croquet and nightly s'mores.
Armstrong Redwoods State Natural Reserve is about a 10-mile drive from the property.
The inn has close relationships with dozens of nearby vineyards, and the concierge can help arrange special tours and tastings.
Many of the Restaurant's ingredients are grown on the Bartolomei family farm.

highlights.text: The Barn Junior Suite has floor-to-ceiling windows, an indoor and outdoor fireplace, a steam shower, heated marble floors and a two-person tub.
Cottages have private entrances and outdoor seating, plus a gas fireplace, steam shower, heated marble floors and deep soaking tub.
The Wellness Barn spa brings together bodywork, seasonal rituals and thoughtful sourcing.
The inn can drive guests around Sonoma in one of its fleet of electric Volvos.
Kitchen waste goes to the hotel's hens, which lay all of the eggs for the property.

considerations.text: The inn is about 15 minutes from Healdsburg, not in town.
WhataHotel notes the secluded rural setting may require a car for exploring nearby towns and attractions.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: The Farmhouse Inn
